title: Business-Class Airfare on a Trip Taken Before the T&E Change
scenario_text:
Cassiopeia Media reimburses employee travel under its Travel & Expense (T&E) Policy.

Version 3 (in effect through 2025-02-28): "Business-class airfare is reimbursable for any single flight segment with scheduled duration of 6 hours or more. Meal per diem is $75 per full travel day."

Version 4 (effective 2025-03-01): "Business-class airfare is reimbursable only for a single flight segment with scheduled duration of 8 hours or more; otherwise economy is reimbursed. Meal per diem is $60 per full travel day." v4 includes a transition clause: "The T&E version in effect on the expense transaction date (the date the expense is incurred) governs reimbursement, regardless of the date the expense report is submitted or approved. Expenses with a transaction date on or before February 28, 2025 are reimbursed under v3."

Concur shows expense report ER-8890 (employee: J. Alvarez) with two line items: (1) Airfare, business class, $2,410, single flight segment scheduled duration 7 hours 5 minutes, Transaction Date 2025-02-26; (2) Meals, 2 full travel days, Transaction Dates 2025-02-26 and 2025-02-27. The report was submitted 2025-03-10 and is pending manager approval.

The manager messages HR shared services on 2025-03-11: "Reviewing ER-8890. The business-class ticket is a 7-hour flight and the trip was late February, but it was submitted in March after the new 8-hour rule. Is the business-class fare reimbursable, and what per diem rate applies to the two meal days?"

Using the policy history, the transition clause, and the Concur record, determine whether the business-class airfare is reimbursable and the applicable per diem rate.
question: Is the business-class airfare on ER-8890 reimbursable, and what per diem rate applies to the two travel days?
